mainTopic: Testing whether the general rules for deciding הלכה between תנאים (like 'ר׳ יהודה vs. ר׳ שמעון, the הלכה follows ר׳ יהודה') are reliable
overview: On the previous amud, the גמרא listed general rules for deciding which תנא the הלכה follows, and רב משרשיא said we do not rely on these rules. On this amud the גמרא tries one proof after another for his claim. Each time it finds an אמורא who gave an explicit ruling in a dispute that the general rule should already decide. It brings rulings by רב on ר׳ שמעון against ר׳ יהודה, both on the three courtyards and on someone who left his house for שבת. Each time it answers that an explicit ruling may just be a local exception. Next comes רב's ruling for ר׳ יהודה against ר׳ מאיר on making an עירוב with one's feet, which the גמרא rejects by saying that perhaps רב alone does not hold of the rules. Then it brings רבי יוחנן's ruling for רבי יוסי against רבי מאיר on the three-month wait before a woman remarries. That proof is rejected because the ruling was needed to exclude שמואל's view that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר in his גזירות. Finally, the גמרא starts a new proof from a ברייתא about dealing with נכרים and a כהן leaving ארץ ישראל. Along the way it explains that the 'cemetery' there is a בית הפרס. The ברייתא ends with a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי שמעון on the three courtyards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting ר׳ שמעון's view that three courtyards with two houses each are enough. It then reports that רב ruled the הלכה like ר׳ שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי שמעון says:] Three courtyards, each with two houses, [are enough]. And רב חמא בר גוריא said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is building a proof for רב משרשיא's claim that the general rules are not reliable. First it shows that רב explicitly ruled like ר׳ שמעון in one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first words are the end of a quotation of ר׳ שמעון's opinion. That opinion is about how small a section can be when it is set aside in an עירוב of a city. The key new fact is רב's ruling in favor of ר׳ שמעון. This ruling is about to be compared against the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...

phrases.english: [Rabbi Shimon says:] three courtyards of two houses [each are enough].
phrases.notes: This is the end of the quoted view of רבי שמעון, which began on the previous amud.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Chama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues a proof that began on the previous amud, searching for a source for רב משרשיא's claim.
steps.raayaObject: רב משרשיא's claim that the general rules for deciding הלכה are not relied upon.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's explicit ruling like ר׳ שמעון in the case of the three courtyards.

steps.title: The ruling clashes with the general rule favoring רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The opponent in this case is ר׳ יהודה. The general rule says the הלכה follows ר׳ יהודה over ר׳ שמעון, so רב's ruling seems to contradict the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who disagrees with him? רבי יהודה. But didn't you say that when רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב's ruling goes against the general rule. It uses this to finish the proof that the rules are not reliable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב had relied on the rule 'ר׳ יהודה over ר׳ שמעון,' he would have ruled like ר׳ יהודה here. Since he ruled the opposite way, it looks as though the rule is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't you say? (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: And who disagrees with him? Rabbi Yehuda.
But didn't you say:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה!
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon: the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This compares רב's ruling from step 1 against the general rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule 'רבי יהודה ורבי שמעון — הלכה כרבי יהודה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ruled against the rule's outcome. This suggests the rule is not authoritative, which supports רב משרשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: This קשיא is not attacking רב. It uses רב's ruling as evidence against the general rule.

steps.title: Rejection: an explicit ruling is just a specific exception
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Where an explicit ruling was given, it applies there. Everywhere else, the general rule still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Perhaps here too, where it was stated, it was stated; where it was not stated, it was not stated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An explicit ruling like ר׳ שמעון can be a specific exception to the rule without cancelling it. In every case where no explicit ruling was given, the rule 'הלכה כרבי יהודה' could still apply. So the proof fails.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? (signals a rejection)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rejection teaches a recurring pattern: an explicit ruling in one place does not disprove a general rule. It may simply be an exception.

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps here too,
where it was stated [explicitly], it was stated,
[and] where it was not stated, it was not stated [so the general rule applies].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This rejects the proof built in steps 1-2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from רב's ruling like ר׳ שמעון.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An explicit ruling may be an exception that does not cancel the general rule elsewhere.

steps.title: New proof: the משנה about someone who leaves his house for Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new proof. It quotes a משנה where ר׳ מאיר says that a person who went away for שבת still restricts his neighbors.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, [the proof is] from what we learned: One who leaves his house and goes to spend שבת in another city, whether a gentile or a Jew, restricts the residents of the courtyard. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first proof failed, the גמרא opens a new attempt. Here it begins quoting a משנה with several opinions, setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a resident who did not join the עירוב חצירות and is away for שבת. According to ר׳ מאיר, his share in the courtyard still forbids the others to carry. The גמרא will use the argument among the תנאים here to test the rules again.

keyTerms.meaning: To spend שבת / establish his שבת residence

phrases.english: Rather, from that which we learned [in a mishna]:
One who leaves his house
and went to spend Shabbat in another city,
whether a gentile or a Jew,
restricts the residents of the courtyards [from carrying],
phrases.notes: This is because he did not join in the עירוב.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This replaces the proof that was rejected in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רב משרשיא's claim that the general rules are not relied upon.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה with the argument of ר׳ מאיר, ר׳ יהודה, ר׳ יוסי and ר׳ שמעון. It is analyzed next.

steps.title: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי: when the absent person does not restrict
steps.stepSummary: ר׳ יהודה says the absent person never restricts. ר׳ יוסי says a gentile restricts but a Jew does not, because a Jew will not come back on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He does not restrict. רבי יוסי says: A gentile restricts, a Jew does not restrict, because it is not the way of a Jew to come [home] on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with two more opinions that disagree with ר׳ מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ר׳ יהודה holds that since the person is away, he does not restrict at all. ר׳ יוסי draws a line. A gentile might come back on שבת, so he still restricts. A Jew who has settled elsewhere for שבת will not come back, so he does not.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He does not restrict.
Rabbi Yosei says:
A gentile restricts; a Jew does not restrict,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין דֶּרֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָבֹא בַּשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: because it is not the way of a Jew to come [back] on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues quoting the משנה that began in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ר׳ יהודה: the absent person does not restrict. ר׳ יוסי: a gentile restricts, a Jew does not.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: even staying in the same town does not restrict
steps.stepSummary: ר׳ שמעון goes furthest. Even if the person only went to his daughter's home in the same town, he does not restrict, because he has put the idea of coming back out of his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Even if he left his house and went to spend שבת with his daughter in the same city, he does not restrict, because he has already removed [returning] from his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with ר׳ שמעון's most lenient opinion. This completes the source that the גמרא will analyze next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case he could easily walk home on שבת. Even so, ר׳ שמעון says he does not restrict. Once he decided to stay elsewhere, he mentally gave up on using his house.

keyTerms.meaning: He removed it from his mind (gave up the idea of returning)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has four views on someone absent for שבת: ר׳ מאיר always restricts; ר׳ יהודה never restricts; ר׳ יוסי restricts for a gentile but not a Jew; ר׳ שמעון does not restrict even if he stays in the same town. The גמרא will use this argument to test the decision rules.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even if he left his house

phrases.aramaic: וְהָלַךְ לִשְׁבּוֹת אֵצֶל בִּתּוֹ בְּאוֹתָהּ הָעִיר —
phrases.english: and went to spend Shabbat with his daughter in the same city,
he does not restrict,
because he has already removed [returning] from his mind.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ הִנִּיחַ אֶת בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes the quotation of the משנה from steps 4-5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ר׳ שמעון: the absent person does not restrict, even if he is staying in the same town, because he has given up the idea of returning.

steps.title: רב rules like ר׳ שמעון in the daughter's-home case
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר גוריא quotes רב: the הלכה follows ר׳ שמעון, and the one who argues with him is ר׳ יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חמא בר גוריא said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows ר׳ שמעון. And who argues with him? ר׳ יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from רב that sides with ר׳ שמעון in the case of the person who left for שבת. This sets up a challenge to the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 brought ר׳ שמעון's view that even someone who went to his daughter's home in the same town does not restrict his neighbors. רב now says the הלכה follows that view. The גמרא points out that the opponent here is ר׳ יהודה, which matters for the next step.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: This refers to רבי שמעון's view in the daughter's-home case.

phrases.english: and who disagrees with him? Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: Naming the opponent sets up the problem in the next step.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב's ruling on the dispute described in steps 5-6.
steps.raayaObject: That the general decision rules cannot be relied on.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's explicit ruling for ר׳ שמעון against ר׳ יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows ר׳ שמעון: a person who went away for שבת, even only to his daughter's home in the same town, does not restrict his neighbors.

steps.title: This ruling contradicts the rule favoring ר׳ יהודה over ר׳ שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Didn't you say that between ר׳ יהודה and ר׳ שמעון the הלכה follows ר׳ יהודה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you say that when ר׳ יהודה and ר׳ שמעון argue, the הלכה follows ר׳ יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב's ruling clashes with the general rule. It uses this clash to suggest the rule is not reliable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule says ר׳ יהודה wins over ר׳ שמעון. Here רב rules for ר׳ שמעון against ר׳ יהודה. So it seems רב does not accept the rule.
steps.confusionAlert: This repeats the exact pattern of step 2, with the same opponent (ר׳ יהודה), but on a different משנה. The case here is someone who left his house for שבת, not the three courtyards.

phrases.english: But didn't you say:
in a dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon,
the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that step 7 conflicts with the general rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The general rule that the הלכה follows ר׳ יהודה over ר׳ שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רב rules for ר׳ שמעון against ר׳ יהודה, he must not hold of the rule.

steps.title: An explicit ruling only covers its own case
steps.stepSummary: What is the difficulty? Where it was said, it was said. Where it was not said, the general rule still applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Maybe here too: where an explicit ruling was stated, it was stated. Where it was not stated, it was not stated, and we use the general rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof the same way it did in step 3. רב's ruling is a specific exception and does not cancel the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An explicit ruling for ר׳ שמעון applies only to this case. In every other dispute between ר׳ יהודה and ר׳ שמעון, we still follow ר׳ יהודה. So the general rule survives.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? (dismisses a proof)

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps here too,
where it was stated, it was stated,
where it was not stated, it was not stated.
phrases.notes: In those cases, the general rule is used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 8, using the same reasoning as step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects this proof entirely. The general rule stays in force.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An explicit exception does not show that the rule is rejected. It shows only that this case is different.
steps.whatToRemember: For the second time, an explicit ruling against the rule is explained as a local exception. The general rule still holds.

steps.title: New proof: a poor person makes an עירוב with his feet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new משנה: a poor person may make an עירוב by walking. ר׳ מאיר says this applies only to a poor person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof comes from what we learned in a משנה: This is what they meant when they said a poor person makes an עירוב with his feet. ר׳ מאיר says: We apply this only to a poor person.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the last proof failed, the גמרא starts a new attempt from a different משנה. Here it brings ר׳ מאיר's opinion, which sets up the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an עירוב תחומין is made by placing bread at a spot. A person can also walk to the spot and declare it his resting place for שבת. ר׳ מאיר allows walking only for a poor person who has no food for two meals.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from what we learned in a משנה (opens a new proof)
Makes an עירוב with his feet, by walking to the spot

phrases.english: Rather, from that which we learned in a mishna:
And this is what they said:
a poor person makes an eiruv with his feet.
phrases.notes: He walks to the spot and declares it his place for שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
We apply this only to a poor person.
phrases.notes: A wealthy person must use bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a new one.
steps.raayaObject: That the general decision rules are not reliable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about making an עירוב with one's feet.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ר׳ מאיר: only a poor person may make an עירוב by walking.

steps.title: ר׳ יהודה: walking works for rich and poor alike
steps.stepSummary: ר׳ יהודה says walking works for both poor and rich. Bread was only allowed to make things easier for the wealthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: ר׳ יהודה says: Both a poor person and a rich person may do this. They allowed an עירוב with bread only to make it easier for the rich person, so he would not have to go out and make an עירוב with his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with ר׳ יהודה, who argues with ר׳ מאיר. The גמרא is still setting up its proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ר׳ יהודה, walking is the basic way to make an עירוב for everyone. Bread is only an extra convenience given to the wealthy. This is the opposite of ר׳ מאיר, who saw walking as a special allowance for the poor.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume bread is the main method according to ר׳ יהודה. For him, walking is the basic method, and bread is the easier substitute.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Both a poor person and a rich person.
They said one makes an eiruv with bread
only to make it easier for the rich person,
so that he need not go out and make an eiruv with his feet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to ר׳ מאיר in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ר׳ יהודה: anyone may make an עירוב by walking. Bread is a convenience for the wealthy.

steps.title: רב tells a student to add that the law follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי taught חייא בר רב, in front of רב, that walking works as an עירוב for both poor and rich. רב told him to finish with: the הלכה follows ר׳ יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי was teaching חייא בר רב in front of רב, and he taught: 'Both a poor person and a rich person can make an עירוב by walking.' רב said to him: 'Finish that teaching by adding: the הלכה follows ר׳ יהודה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. רב personally rules that the הלכה follows ר׳ יהודה in the walking-עירוב argument, and this sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step, ר׳ יהודה said walking works for rich and poor alike, while ר׳ מאיר limited it to a poor person. Here רב explicitly says the הלכה follows ר׳ יהודה. That explicit ruling is the raw material the גמרא will now question.

keyTerms.meaning: Was teaching or reciting a teaching
In front of רב, in his presence
Both a poor person and a rich person
Also finish it with this, add this at the end

phrases.aramaic: וּמַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: And Rav Chiya bar Ashi was teaching
phrases.notes: A teacher reviewing the law with a student.

phrases.english: to Chiya the son of Rav, in front of Rav:
phrases.notes: רב himself was present, so his reaction counts as his own ruling.

phrases.english: Both a poor person and a rich person (may make an eruv by walking).
phrases.notes: This is ר׳ יהודה's position from the previous step.

phrases.english: And Rav said to him,
Also finish it with this:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: An explicit ruling for this specific argument.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי לְחִיָּיא בַּר רַב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב's explicit ruling on the argument between ר׳ מאיר and ר׳ יהודה brought in steps 10-11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: in walking-עירוב, the הלכה follows ר׳ יהודה (it works for rich and poor alike).

steps.title: Why say it twice if the general rule already decides?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed a special ruling. The general rule already says that between ר׳ מאיר and ר׳ יהודה, the הלכה follows ר׳ יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need two rulings? Didn't you already say that when ר׳ מאיר and ר׳ יהודה argue, the הלכה follows ר׳ יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's extra ruling. If the general rule already covers this case, saying it again seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule should automatically decide this argument for ר׳ יהודה. Since רב bothered to say it out loud, it looks as if the general rule is not accepted. If it were accepted, why would רב need to spell it out?

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need two (statements)? Why say it twice?

phrases.english: Why do I need two?
phrases.notes: Two rulings: the general rule and רב's specific ruling.

phrases.english: But didn't you say:
Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda (when they argue) —
the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda!
phrases.notes: This is the general rule (כלל) the גמרא is checking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב's explicit ruling to suggest that the general rule is not accepted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The general rule that between ר׳ מאיר and ר׳ יהודה, the הלכה follows ר׳ יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the general rule were accepted, רב's specific ruling would be unnecessary. Since he made one anyway, the rule seems not to be accepted.

steps.title: Maybe only רב rejects the rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the proof. Maybe רב personally does not hold of these general rules, which says nothing about whether others accept them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Maybe רב just doesn't hold of these general rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down its own proof from step 13. It says the proof is too weak to show anything about the rules in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 showed, at most, that רב needed to say the ruling. That could simply mean רב personally does not use these rules. Other חכמים might still accept them, so the גמרא looks for another proof, starting in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? (signals pushing a question away)
He does not hold of it, does not accept it
General rules (here, the rules for deciding הלכה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is trying to find out רב's personal view. The real goal is whether the general rules are accepted at all. That is why showing something about רב alone does not settle the question.

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא רַב לֵית לֵיהּ לְהָנֵי כְּלָלֵי?
phrases.english: Perhaps Rav does not accept these general rules?
phrases.notes: Other חכמים may still accept them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי קוּשְׁיָא? דִּילְמָא רַב לֵית לֵיהּ לְהָנֵי כְּלָלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רב's ruling as proof about whether the general rules are accepted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof only shows something about רב personally, not about the rules as generally accepted.

steps.title: A new proof begins from the law of a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new proof from a משנה: a יבמה may not do חליצה or יבום until three months have passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we learn it from this משנה: A יבמה may not do חליצה and may not do יבום until three months have passed (since her husband's death).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the רב proof and opens a new one from a different משנה. This step only quotes the beginning of that משנה and sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows the earlier line of proof has been abandoned. The משנה about a יבמה, who waits three months to see whether she is pregnant from her late husband, will be used to test the general rules. The actual argument comes in the next part of the משנה and the discussion after it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous approach and starts a new one)
From this that we learned in a משנה
A widow whose husband died without children and who waits for her brother-in-law
The ceremony that frees the יבמה from her brother-in-law

phrases.english: Rather, (prove it) from that which we learned (in a mishna):
phrases.notes: The new proof begins here.

phrases.english: The yevama may not do chalitza and may not do yibum
phrases.notes: Neither option is allowed yet.

phrases.english: until she has had three months (since her husband's death).
phrases.notes: Waiting shows whether she is pregnant. If she is, she is exempt from both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 14 rejected the proof from רב, the גמרא turns to a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the general rules for deciding הלכה are accepted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a יבמה waiting three months before חליצה or יבום.

steps.title: All other women must also wait three months
steps.stepSummary: The משנה extends the three-month wait to all women whose marriage or engagement ended. They may not marry or even get engaged, no matter what their status was.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same goes for all other women: they may not marry and may not even get engaged until three months have passed. This applies to virgins and non-virgins, widows and divorcees, and to women who were only engaged or fully married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the משנה it started in step 15. This is the first opinion (the תנא קמא), which sets up the מחלוקת that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 covered a יבמה, and now the משנה says the same three-month wait applies to every woman. The main reason for the wait is to make sure we know who the father of any baby is. The חכמים made one rule for everyone, even in cases where that worry seems unlikely.

keyTerms.meaning: Three months: the waiting period, so we can tell whether she is already pregnant
Women who were only engaged (had אירוסין, the first stage of marriage)
Women who were fully married (had נישואין)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic in מסכת עירובין. The גמרא is quoting a משנה from יבמות only to test the general rules about whose opinion is followed in הלכה.

phrases.english: And similarly, all other women
may not be married and may not be betrothed
phrases.notes: Even the engagement is forbidden, not only the marriage

phrases.english: until three months have passed for them
whether virgins or non-virgins
whether widows or divorcees
whether betrothed or married

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן שְׁאָר כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים לֹא יִנָּשְׂאוּ וְלֹא יִתְאָרְסוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same משנה that step 15 began as a new proof source
steps.raayaObject: Whether the general rules of הלכה (such as following רבי יהודה over רבי מאיר) are accepted
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in יבמות about the three-month waiting period
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: every woman waits three months before marriage or אירוסין

steps.title: רבי יהודה lets some women get engaged or marry right away
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a formerly married woman may get engaged immediately, and a formerly engaged woman may marry immediately. The exception is an engaged woman in יהודה, because couples there spent time alone during the engagement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: women who were married may get engaged right away. Women who were only engaged may marry right away. The exception is an engaged woman in יהודה, because there the groom was comfortable and familiar with her.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the quoted משנה, רבי יהודה disagrees with the תנא קמא and allows a shorter path in certain cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reasons that an engaged couple normally does not live together. So a married woman can get engaged right away (she still waits to marry), and an engaged woman can marry right away, since she could not be pregnant. In יהודה, engaged couples were alone together, so the worry of pregnancy comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: An engaged woman in the region of יהודה, where the custom was different
His heart is bold with her: the groom felt familiar enough that they may have lived together

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Married women may be betrothed
phrases.notes: Right away, since nothing physical happens during אירוסין

phrases.english: and betrothed women may be married
phrases.notes: Right away, since they were never living with the first man

phrases.english: except for a betrothed woman in Judea
because his heart is bold with her

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing opinion to the תנא קמא of step 16, within the same quoted משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a married woman may get engaged right away and an engaged woman may marry right away, except an engaged woman in יהודה

steps.title: רבי יוסי lets all women get engaged except a widow
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says every woman may get engaged right away. Only a widow must wait, because she is still mourning her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: all women may get engaged right away, except a widow, because of her mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted משנה ends with a third opinion, from רבי יוסי. With this, the גמרא has finished laying out the source it will use for its next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the three-month rule applies only to actually marrying, so any woman may get engaged right away. The widow is held back for a different reason: out of respect for her mourning, not because of worry about pregnancy. The גמרא will soon identify רבי יוסי's real opponent as רבי מאיר and use that pairing to test the general rules of הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Mourning: the widow's grief for her husband who died

steps.whyThisMatters: The general rules say that in a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. Once רבי מאיר is shown to be the opponent (step 21), the גמרא can ask why רבי יוחנן needed an explicit ruling here (step 22).
steps.confusionAlert: The widow's wait for רבי יוסי has nothing to do with pregnancy. It is only because of mourning, which is a different reason from the rest of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
All the women may be betrothed
phrases.notes: Right away

phrases.english: except for the widow
because of the mourning

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים יִתְאָרְסוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion to the quoted משנה, finishing the source the גמרא will use for its proof
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: all women may get engaged right away, except a widow, because of mourning

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: A story: רבי אליעזר missed the בית מדרש, and רבי אסי told him that רבי יוחנן ruled the הלכה follows רבי יוסי in the three-month-wait case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said about this: רבי אליעזר did not go to the study hall. He found רבי אסי standing and asked him, 'What did they say in the study hall?' He answered, 'This is what רבי יוחנן said: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its proof by telling a story in which רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יוסי on the three-month wait. This sets up the key question that comes later: why did רבי יוחנן need to say this at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling refers to the lenient opinion of רבי יוסי from step 18, that women may get engaged right away. The proof will depend on the fact that רבי יוחנן felt he had to state this ruling openly.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law follows רבי יוסי

phrases.english: And we said (regarding this):

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא עָל לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer did not go into the study hall.
He found Rabbi Asi, who was standing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי אֲמוּר בְּבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא?
phrases.english: He said to him: What did they say in the study hall?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אֲמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי יוסי's lenient view from step 18.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמְרִינַן: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לָא עָל לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings רבי יוחנן's ruling on the dispute laid out in steps 15-18.
steps.raayaObject: That the general rules for deciding הלכה are not accepted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's explicit ruling like רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Does a single תנא argue with רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks whether the ruling implies that one individual תנא disagrees with רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that imply that a single authority disagrees with him?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר asks a clarifying question. If the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, who is the one person arguing against him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי seems to stand against several other opinions, and normally the הלכה does not follow one authority against many. So רבי אליעזר infers that רבי יוחנן's ruling means only a single authority really disagrees with him, and asks whether that is correct.

phrases.english: By implication, does a single authority disagree with him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details behind רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the single opponent of רבי יוסי in this case?

steps.title: רבי מאיר is the one who disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes a ברייתא. רבי מאיר requires a three-month wait even when there is no chance of pregnancy, while רבי יוסי allows these women to get engaged and married immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. A ברייתא teaches: if a woman was eager to go to her father's house, or was angry with her husband, or her husband was old or sick, or she was sick, barren, old, a minor, or an אילונית, or otherwise unable to give birth, or her husband was in prison, or she miscarried after her husband died, all of them must wait three months. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי permits them to get engaged and to marry immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers 'yes' and shows that the one who argues is רבי מאיר. He proves it with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the cases in the ברייתא are women who almost certainly cannot be pregnant from the first husband. רבי מאיר still makes them wait, because the rule applies to everyone. רבי יוסי says no wait is needed when the reason for the rule does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is physically unable to bear children

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this רבי יוסי with his view in step 18 about a widow. Here the ברייתא lists cases where pregnancy is not a real concern, and רבי יוסי allows even marriage right away.

phrases.english: Yes, and it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיְתָה רְדוּפָה לֵילֵךְ לְבֵית אָבִיהָ,
phrases.english: If she was eager to go to her father's house,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיְתָה לָהּ כַּעַס עִם בַּעְלָהּ,
phrases.english: or she was angry with her husband,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּעְלָהּ זָקֵן אוֹ חוֹלֶה,
phrases.english: or her husband was old or sick,
or she herself was sick,
barren, elderly, a minor, or an aylonit,
or one who is not able to give birth,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּעְלָהּ חָבוּשׁ בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: or her husband was locked in prison,
a woman who miscarried after her husband's death
all of them must wait three months,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַתִּיר לֵיאָרֵס וְלִינָּשֵׂא מִיָּד.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei permits them to become engaged and to marry immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רבי מאיר is the single opponent, as the ברייתא shows.

steps.title: Why did רבי יוחנן need to say it?
steps.stepSummary: If the general rule 'רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי' were accepted, רבי יוחנן's ruling would be unnecessary. So the general rules are apparently not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this ruling? Didn't you say that in a dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the main point of the proof. רבי יוחנן's statement would be extra if the general rule already settled the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן still needed to state 'הלכה כרבי יוסי' openly. This suggests the general rule cannot be relied on, which supports the idea that the general rules are not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (the statement seems unnecessary)

phrases.english: Why do I need this?
But didn't you say:
In a dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei,
the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רבי יוחנן's ruling, now that we know רבי מאיר is the opponent.
steps.raayaObject: That the general rules for deciding הלכה are not accepted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's apparently unnecessary ruling like רבי יוסי against רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ruling was needed against שמואל's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי יוחנן's ruling may have been needed to exclude שמואל's rule that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר in his גזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Perhaps the ruling comes to exclude what רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי מאיר in his גזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 22. It shows that רבי יוחנן's statement had a real purpose even if the general rule is accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's three-month wait for every woman is a גזירה, a protective decree. שמואל holds that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר in his גזירות, so without רבי יוחנן's statement we might have ruled like רבי מאיר here. רבי יוחנן's ruling is therefore not extra, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difficulty? (a rejection)

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from רבי יוחנן fails. His ruling may simply be teaching that רבי יוסי wins here, even though רבי מאיר's view is a גזירה, against שמואל's rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a 'why do I need this?' proof breaks down if the statement can be explained as excluding a competing rule.

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps it comes to exclude
what Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel,
who said: The halacha follows Rabbi Meir in his decrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling is not extra. It was needed to exclude שמואל's rule that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר in his גזירות.

steps.title: A new proof begins: buying from gentiles at their fair
steps.stepSummary: After the last proof was rejected, the גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It allows buying animals, slaves, and land from נכרים at their fair, and registering the deeds in their courts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof comes from this ברייתא: A person may go to a fair of נכרים and buy from them animals, slaves, and maidservants, and also houses, fields, and vineyards. He may write the deeds and have them confirmed in their courts, because he is like someone rescuing property from their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the old proof and starts quoting a new ברייתא, which will be the source of a new proof. This step is setting up the next move. The important part for the proof has not come yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the earlier proof failed (step 23) and a new source is coming. The ברייתא allows things that might seem forbidden, such as going to an idolatrous fair and using נכרי courts. It justifies this because the buyer is 'rescuing' things from נכרי hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Here it signals a new attempt after the previous proof was rejected.
A fair or market held by נכרים, often tied to idol worship
He writes the deed and has it officially confirmed
As if rescuing it from their hands

steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for the proof inside this paragraph. This is only the opening of a long ברייתא. The point that matters for the question about the general rules comes later in it.

phrases.english: Rather, from that which was taught:
phrases.notes: A new proof replaces the rejected one.

phrases.english: One may go to a fair of gentiles
and buy animals from them
phrases.notes: Buying them moves them into Jewish ownership.

phrases.english: and slaves and maidservants,
phrases.notes: Bought slaves enter a state of מצוה obligation.

phrases.english: houses, fields, and vineyards,
phrases.notes: This is for the sake of settling ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: and he may write deeds and have them confirmed in their courts,
because it is as though he is rescuing it from their hands.
phrases.notes: The court's seal stops the sellers from backing out of the sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof rejected in step 23 with a new source.
steps.raayaObject: That the general rules for deciding between תנאים are not accepted
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about doing business with נכרים (the relevant part comes later in it)

steps.title: A כהן may become impure to protect his property
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. A כהן may become טמא by leaving ארץ ישראל to litigate with נכרים, and likewise by entering a cemetery.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he is a כהן, he may become טמא by going outside ארץ ישראל in order to bring his case against them and to contest their claims. And just as he may become טמא outside ארץ ישראל, so may he become טמא in a cemetery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא. It now adds a rule for a כהן: he may become טמא in order to defend his property from נכרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land outside ארץ ישראל is טמא by a rabbinic decree, so the חכמים could relax that decree for a good purpose like this. But the ברייתא then extends the leniency to a 'cemetery'. That extension sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest, who is normally forbidden to become טמא from the dead
Outside ארץ ישראל, which the חכמים declared impure
To litigate and to contest claims

phrases.english: And if he is a priest —
he may become impure by going outside the Land
phrases.notes: The impurity of land outside ארץ ישראל is rabbinic.

phrases.english: to litigate and contest with them.
And just as he may become impure outside the Land —
so may he become impure in a cemetery.
phrases.notes: This is the line the גמרא is about to question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Continuation of the proof's source text

steps.title: How can a כהן be allowed into a real cemetery?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses the ברייתא in surprise. A cemetery causes טומאה דאורייתא, so how could the חכמים permit a כהן to enter it?
steps.simpleTranslation: A cemetery? Could that enter your mind? That is impurity from the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops the quote to challenge the last line of the ברייתא. A rabbinic leniency cannot permit something the Torah forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים may relax their own decrees, such as the impurity of land outside ארץ ישראל. A real cemetery, though, makes a כהן טמא by Torah law. Protecting property cannot override a Torah prohibition, so the ברייתא as written seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? An expression of surprise
Ritual impurity that comes from Torah law

phrases.english: A cemetery, can it enter your mind?!
It is impurity by Torah law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the final clause of the ברייתא quoted in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a כהן may become טמא in a cemetery
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cemetery impurity is from the Torah, and a rabbinic-level reason such as protecting property cannot permit a Torah prohibition.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a field of uncertain graves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'cemetery' here means a בית הפרס, a plowed-over field where bones may be scattered. Its טומאה is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means a בית הפרס, whose impurity is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own challenge by reading 'cemetery' as a בית הפרס. A בית הפרס is only rabbinically טמא, so the חכמים could allow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית הפרס is a field in which a grave was plowed over, so bones might be scattered through it. The חכמים declared it טמא, so they can permit it for an important need. This fits the same logic as the rabbinic impurity of land outside ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was plowed over, impure only by rabbinic law
From the חכמים, meaning rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא allows a כהן to become טמא only where the טומאה is דרבנן: land outside ארץ ישראל and a בית הפרס. A real cemetery, which is טומאה דאורייתא, is not permitted.

phrases.english: Rather, it means a field of plowed-over graves,
which is impure only by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 26 by reinterpreting the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a term in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Cemetery' means an actual cemetery, which is טומאה דאורייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Cemetery' means a בית הפרס, which is only טמא מדרבנן, so the חכמים could permit it.

steps.title: A כהן may leave the land to marry or to learn תורה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that a כהן may become טמא by leaving ארץ ישראל in order to marry a woman or to learn תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a כהן may become impure by leaving the land in order to marry a woman and in order to learn תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the same ברייתא it brought as proof. Now the ברייתא lists two more reasons a כהן may leave ארץ ישראל: to get married and to learn תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טומאה of land outside ארץ ישראל is only a rabbinic decree. So the חכמים allowed a כהן to set it aside for important מצוה needs. Marriage and תורה learning are added to the earlier cases of business dealings with נכרים and litigating against them.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes ritually impure (here, by leaving ארץ ישראל)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not mean a כהן walks into a real grave. The 'impurity' here comes from leaving ארץ ישראל, and that is only a rabbinic טומאה.

phrases.english: And he may become impure in order to marry a woman,
phrases.notes: By going out to חוץ לארץ, which the חכמים declared טמא.

phrases.english: and in order to learn Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the clarification that the 'cemetery' is only a בית הפרס, the ברייתא resumes with more מצוה reasons that permit rabbinic טומאה.
steps.raayaObject: That the general rules for deciding הלכה between תנאים are not accepted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuing ברייתא about a כהן leaving ארץ ישראל

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits the permission to learn
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a כהן may leave ארץ ישראל to learn only if he cannot find a place to learn there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When is this allowed? When he cannot find a place to learn. But if he can find a place to learn, he may not make himself impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a condition to the permission to leave the land for learning. It applies only when there is no place to learn in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the permission exists only out of real need. If the כהן can learn תורה without leaving, there is no reason to set aside the rabbinic טומאה, so it stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: When? (introduces a limitation of a rule)
Finds a place or teacher to learn from

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: When does this apply?
At a time when he cannot find a place to learn,
phrases.notes: Meaning in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: but if he finds a place to learn, he may not become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the תורה-learning permission just stated in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן may leave ארץ ישראל to learn only if no place to learn exists there.

steps.title: רבי יוסי permits leaving even when there is a place to learn
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees and allows the כהן to leave even when he can learn in ארץ ישראל. He then begins to give his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Even when he finds a place to learn, he may also become impure, because...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי argues with רבי יהודה and permits leaving even when there is a place to learn at home. The amud ends in the middle of his reason, which is finished on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that a place to learn at home is not enough to forbid leaving. The word לפי ('because') shows that a reason is coming. That reason will explain why going elsewhere to learn can still be justified.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַף בִּזְמַן שֶׁמּוֹצֵא לִלְמוֹד —
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: Even at a time when he finds a place to learn,
he may also become impure, because
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַף בִּזְמַן שֶׁמּוֹצֵא לִלְמוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי יהודה's limitation and opens the opposing view inside the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן may leave ארץ ישראל to learn even when a place to learn exists there. The reason follows on the next amud.
